A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HOT research, with matching foundational mathematics and overlapping experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting and MedMNIST3D classification results, attention ablations, efficiency measurements, and five-seed evaluations.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for HOT variants on forecasting, medical classification, and multispectral segmentation, together with ablations, efficiency measurements, and attention analyses.

M1.justification: v1's final method combines Kronecker-product attention with Performer kernelization. v2 removes that kernelized stage and introduces normalized Kronecker-sum attention alongside softmax-based product attention, changing value aggregation (Section 4.2). It also replaces the multilayer medical-image convolutional encoder with a single patch convolution and introduces an unpooled segmentation output head.

E1.justification: v2 adds satellite-image segmentation using SSL4EO-L OLI/TIRS-RS imagery with NLCD and CDL labels, substantially extending domain and task coverage. Conversely, Exchange forecasting and SynapseMNIST3D classification are removed from both the main experiments and appendices.

E2.justification: The forecasting comparisons remove SCINet, Stationary, TiDE, RLinear, and DLinear and add a temporal Transformer; iTransformer remains under the name Transformer (spatial). Medical comparisons remove Auto-sklearn, Auto-Keras, DWT-CV, and the separately labeled ResNet configurations, while adding ViT-3D, ViViT-S, TimeSformer, and MViT. Non-factorized attention already appeared in v1's ablations and is retained and expanded in v2's main comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported tuning design changes from searching 1–4 blocks and widths 64/128/256 to fixed task-specific depths and width 128, with revised patch, head-count, pooling, and weight-decay settings (v1 Table 9; v2 Table 6). v2 also introduces standardized FLOP measurements, inference profiling, and segmentation protocols comparing scratch-trained HOT with MoCo-pretrained baselines. Retained forecasting splits and horizons remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds stable-rank tracking, positional-encoding and FFN-removal ablations, comparative efficiency analyses, and ECL attention-map studies. The head-count study is expanded to product, sum, and non-factorized models. v1's attention-order and factorization-versus-kernelization studies are largely removed, although its no-attention forecasting control survives in v2 Table 8 and full-attention comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five random seeds for forecasting and medical classification (v1 Tables 10–11; v2 Tables 9–10). Changed variant coverage, horizon aggregation, and numerical uncertainties do not establish a different statistical procedure. Neither version reports confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Main result rows are extensively replaced: ECL MSE is 0.172 for v1 HOT versus 0.169/0.167 for v2 product/sum, while Vessel AUC is 97.6 versus 85.7/84.9. These concern revised methods/settings, not established same-setting gains or losses. v2 adds segmentation, rank, and efficiency outcomes, changes some retained baseline scores, and removes v1's detailed per-horizon forecasting results.

T1.justification: v2 adds Kronecker-sum definitions, row-stochasticity theorems and proofs, stable-rank formulas and bounds, and Tucker/tensor-train formulations (Sections 3–4 and Appendix A). The original Kronecker-product universality theorem and CP-based proof are retained and relocated, with additional qualifications on their architectural interpretation. v1's kernel-attention derivation is removed.

C1.justification: The principal contribution shifts from kernelized, linearly scaling HOT to a product/sum framework for dense and sparse multidimensional dependencies. v2 emphasizes rank-controlled expressiveness and presents learned attention-map interpretability as an achieved contribution, whereas v1 leaves attention-map analysis to future work. The original linear-attention contribution is no longer claimed.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits universality to sums of Kronecker products, discusses separability and alternative factorizations, and interprets stable-rank behavior, positional encodings, and attention-map patterns. These replace substantial discussion of kernelization and attention order. Its broader-impact statement additionally qualifies clinical generalization and real-world interpretability as unestablished by the benchmark evaluations.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code release; v2 supplies a concrete public implementation URL. v2 revises architecture and hyperparameter documentation, adds segmentation preprocessing, splits, and output-head details, specifies GPU memory, CPU, and RAM, and identifies borrowed versus reproduced baseline results. Conversely, v1's standalone algorithm pseudocode is removed. The linked implementation was not externally checked.

R1.justification: v2 substantially reframes HOT through multiway analysis and Kronecker covariance modeling, adding discussion of work by Tsiligkaridis and Hero, Greenewald and Hero, Song, and Wang. Related work also expands to video Transformers, neural-network tensorization, SegFormer3D, and Tensor Product Attention. This changes the research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the expanded framework. Section 4 is reorganized into generalization, decomposition, architecture, and theoretical analysis; the appendices are restructured around theory, datasets, baseline descriptions, and additional experiments. This is substantial narrative revision beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: The architecture diagram is redrawn, and the visual presentation adds stable-rank curves, revised head-count plots, efficiency charts, and extensive attention-map grids. Main tables replace asymptotic-complexity columns with GFLOPS and separate product/sum rows. Older ablation displays and the detailed forecasting table disappear, while uncertainty tables are consolidated and figures increasingly use wrapped-text layouts.

improvement.justification: v2 adds broader validation, useful ablations, attention visualizations, and a concrete implementation link. However, its new stable-rank argument uses trace and singular-value bounds that do not hold for general row-stochastic matrices (Section 4.4.1, Eqs. 14–15). New reporting inconsistencies include 4.3M segmentation parameters in Table 3 versus 1M in the discussion, and detailed forecasting results are lost. These reliability problems affect theoretical and efficiency claims, leaving the net benefit of the substantial additions uncertain.
